# Tradebook

A profession companion for **World of Warcraft: Forever**.

> For WoW Forever 1.60.1. Please report problems on GitHub.

## Features

- A profession window laid out like the modern Professions window (recipe list on the left, details on the right). It replaces the default window, with a one-click switch back to the default UI.
- A bottom tab for every Forever profession, plus a **Camp** tab for campsite recipes.
- Crafting from Tradebook for the character you're logged into: Craft, quantity, Craft All.
- Every character's professions, skill levels and known recipes saved account-wide, with a fast **"Who can craft this?"** search.
- Reagent counts from bags and bank, missing-reagent highlights, an expandable reagent tree with the nearest vendors for each material, and shopping lists split into vendor and auction house.
- A **leveling plan**: a sure way to a profession's skill cap (orange recipes, cheapest first), with materials, cost and a shopping list.
- Where to get every recipe in Forever: trainers, vendors (with Merchant's Favor costs and reputation), the mobs that drop it with drop chances, world drops and quests; and the vendor price next to the auction house price.
- A **Vendors** tab: search any item a vendor sells, nearest vendors first, with prices and waypoints. It ships with a community database of vendors and trainers scanned in game, and the vendors and trainers you open are scanned and shared in game with other Tradebook users (NPC data only; can be turned off).
- **Train the next rank**: when a character can train Journeyman, Expert or Artisan, the requirements, cost, and the trainers, books or quests that teach it in Forever. Specializations (Gnomish/Goblin Engineering, Dragonscale/Elemental/Tribal Leatherworking) too.
- **Browse any profession**, even one none of your characters have, and see which of your characters **could learn** a recipe.
- A Camp tab for campsite recipes across all your characters.
- A read-only view of your Legacy profession perks.
- Friends' profession ranks if you use Fellowship Ledger, and where to farm materials if you use Questie.
- A minimap button and a Data Broker launcher.

## Optional addons

Tradebook works on its own; these add more when installed:

- **Questie**: vendors nobody has scanned yet, the mobs and gathering nodes for each material, and the nearest trainers and vendors for unlearned recipes, with waypoints (click an NPC nearby to target and mark it).
- **TomTom**: waypoints use TomTom's arrow (otherwise the game's map pin).
- **Fellowship Ledger**: friends' profession ranks.
- **Auctionator**: auction and vendor prices for materials, the cost to craft, what the result sells for and the profit (at auction or to a vendor), a profit column in the recipe list, and sending a shopping list to Auctionator.

## Help build the vendor database

Tradebook shares the vendors and trainers you open with other Tradebook users in game, on a hidden channel (setting on by default; `/tb net` for status; see [docs/DATA.md](https://github.com/TankerALane/Tradebook/blob/main/docs/DATA.md), "In-game sharing"). What your copy hears is exported by the maintainer's "import npc data" step. Or type `/tb share` in game, copy the text and paste it into the [Vendor data form](https://github.com/TankerALane/Tradebook/issues/new?template=vendor-data.yml). Shares are merged with `python -I scripts/merge_vendor_shares.py --issues` into `Tradebook/Data/CommunityVendors.lua` for the next release. Only vendor data is shared.

## Install

Install from CurseForge (search "Tradebook"), or download the zip from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/TankerALane/Tradebook/releases) and extract the `Tradebook` folder into `World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns`.

## Credits

- Developed by **Decoupled Lane Studio**.
- Recipe source data adapted from **LibProfessionDB** by Pmptasty (MIT License).
- Classic disenchanting table from the **Warcraft Wiki** "Disenchanting tables" page (CC BY-SA 4.0), shown as classic until confirmed in WoW Forever.
- Skill-up ranges from WoW Forever's game data (via wago.tools).

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](https://github.com/TankerALane/Tradebook/blob/main/LICENSE). Embedded libraries keep their own licenses.

## v1.11.0

### Professions tab
- **Find a trainer for a free profession slot**: click an empty primary slot for the nearest trainer of each primary profession you could still learn; click one for a waypoint. A secondary profession you haven't learned shows its nearest trainer in its tooltip; right-click it for a waypoint. (Needs Questie; trainers not seen in game are marked unconfirmed.)

## v1.10.2

### Data
- New vendors: Morhan Coppertongue, Joshua Maclure, Vharr, Hragran, Uthok, Aldren Cordon, Krakk, Rann Flamespinner, Terry Palin, Micha Yance, Sly Garrett, Jutak, Glyx Brewright, Moodan Sungrain, Bhaldaran Ravenshade, Innkeeper Thulbek, Kurgul, Tarban Hearthgrain, Jang, Pix Xizzix and Daniel Stitchsong. 643 vendors, 8,764 items.
- New trainers: Pyall Silentstride (Cooking), Mishiki (Herbalism), Malux (Skinning) and Lui'Mala (Fishing). 182 trainers, 3,208 services.
- Disenchanting: 256 disenchants in 13 bands.

## v1.10.1

### Data
- New vendors: Gunder Thornbush, Lohgan Eva, Tandaan Lightmane, Chylina, My'lanna, Christi Galvanis, Brinna Valanaar, Abra Cadabra and Huey Sunnydale. 622 vendors, 8,369 items.
- Disenchanting: 210 disenchants in 13 bands.

## v1.10.0

### Data
- New vendors: Xizk Goodstitch (Stranglethorn Vale), Morgum and Rekkul (Orgrimmar), Nargal Deatheye and Gishah (The Barrens), Wallace the Blind (Silverpine Forest), Innkeeper Fizzgrimble (Tanaris), Hae'Wilani (Desolace), Vayn Moongaze, Barkeep Hann, Samor Festivus, Kelsey Yance, Mazk Snipeshot, Nixxrax Fillamug, Synge, Kzixx, Laer Stepperunner, Nizzik, Krinkle Goodsteel, Magus Tirth and Mister Graphed. 613 vendors, 8,225 items.
- New trainers: Grarnik Goodstitch (Tailoring, Stranglethorn Vale), Tepa (Tailoring, Thunder Bluff), Arnok (First Aid, Orgrimmar), Telurinon Moonshadow, Myizz Luckycatch, Fremal Doohickey and James Van Brunt. 178 trainers, 3,185 services.
- Disenchanting: 196 disenchants in 13 bands.
- **Disenchant results from one player's several characters count as one player.** Disenchants are saved for the whole account, so each of a player's characters sent the same totals and counted as another player; one player alone could make a band look confirmed. Identical totals now count once, in game and in the shipped data, and so do totals a player's characters sent at different times (3 or more bands exactly alike): only the biggest counts.

### Options
- **K opens on Professions**: a new option. On (the default), the K key opens Tradebook on the Professions tab as before. Off, K opens it on the tab you had open last (or on the profession whose window is open).

### Recipe list
- **Crafted item filters**: the recipe list's Filter menu can now narrow recipes by what they make, like the auction house: **only items this character can use**, **rarity** and **required level** (in steps of 5). Recipes that make no item, like enchants, are left out while one of these is chosen.
- **Pick several rarities or level ranges** (recipe list and Vendors tab): tick as many as you like, e.g. Uncommon and Rare, or 21-25 and 26-30. **Select all** at the top ticks them all, or clears them when they're all ticked. (The Vendors tab's rarity was "at least" one rarity; a saved choice carries over.)
- **Have materials > Except vendor items**: a new filter option that shows the recipes you have the gathered or crafted materials for, where only what a vendor sells (thread, vials, spices...) is missing. Recipes made only of vendor materials aren't shown. Herbs and other materials some vendors sell only a few of (limited stock) count as gathered, not as vendor items.

## v1.9.2

### Data

- New trainers: Telonis (Leatherworking, Darnassus), Therum Deepforge (Blacksmithing, Stormwind), Rand Rhobart (Skinning, Tirisfal Glades) and Lawrence Schneider (Tailoring, Stormwind). 171 trainers, 2,993 services.
- Disenchanting: 144 disenchants in 12 bands.

## v1.9.1

### Vendors
- **Questie's vendor lists are checked against real vendor windows**: when a vendor's window has been read (by you, in the community data, or by 2+ players sharing in game) and an item isn't in it, Questie's claim that the vendor sells it is no longer shown (e.g. Burkrum in Ashenvale doesn't sell Razor Arrow). Recipes and items with limited stock are kept, since they may just have been sold out.

### Data
- New vendors: Nerrist and Nargatt (Stranglethorn Vale), K'waii, Kzan Thornslash, Uhgar, Jark, Flakk, Tai'tasi and Trayexir (Durotar), Kixxle and Naela Trance (Wetlands), Jin'sora (Orgrimmar), Tamelyn Aldridge (Redridge Mountains) and Fizzix Boomshot. 557 vendors, 7,382 items.
- New trainers: Una and Tarn (Leatherworking) and Bena Winterhoof (Alchemy) in Thunder Bluff, Arthur Moore (Leatherworking) and Doctor Herbert Halsey (Alchemy) in Undercity, Yarr Hammerstone (Mining, Dun Morogh), Simon Tanner (Leatherworking, Stormwind), and Cook Torka (Cooking) and Rawrk (First Aid) in Durotar. 167 trainers, 2,839 services.
- Disenchanting: 83 disenchants in 12 bands.

## v1.9.0

### Professions tab
- **A new Professions tab**, like the game's Professions book: your two primary profession slots (a blank box while one is free) and your secondary professions (Cooking, First Aid, Fishing; greyed out until learned), each with a large icon, rank and skill bar. Click one to open it, or drag it to an action bar for its spell (Alchemy, Cooking, Smelting for Mining...). Herbalism and Mining also have a smaller Find Herbs / Find Minerals icon at the right, above the skill bar: click it to start tracking (not in combat), or drag it on its own. The red Unlearn cross moved here too, next to the skill bar in each primary profession's box (it still opens the game's pop-up where you type UNLEARN). These replace the spell icons that were on each profession's tab, which leaves more room for the recipe list. The K key (and the profession micro button) always opens Tradebook on it. The minimap button and /tb open on it too when no profession window is open; turn that off in the options to open on the tab you had last.
- **Side tabs**: Professions, Characters, Legacy and Vendors are now icon tabs down the right side of the window (their name shows when you hover over them), which leaves the bottom row to the professions.

## v1.10.0

### Data
- New vendors: Xizk Goodstitch (Stranglethorn Vale), Morgum and Rekkul (Orgrimmar), Nargal Deatheye and Gishah (The Barrens), Wallace the Blind (Silverpine Forest), Innkeeper Fizzgrimble (Tanaris), Hae'Wilani (Desolace), Vayn Moongaze, Barkeep Hann, Samor Festivus, Kelsey Yance, Mazk Snipeshot, Nixxrax Fillamug, Synge, Kzixx, Laer Stepperunner, Nizzik, Krinkle Goodsteel, Magus Tirth and Mister Graphed. 613 vendors, 8,225 items.
- New trainers: Grarnik Goodstitch (Tailoring, Stranglethorn Vale), Tepa (Tailoring, Thunder Bluff), Arnok (First Aid, Orgrimmar), Telurinon Moonshadow, Myizz Luckycatch, Fremal Doohickey and James Van Brunt. 178 trainers, 3,185 services.
- Disenchanting: 196 disenchants in 13 bands.
- **Disenchant results from one player's several characters count as one player.** Disenchants are saved for the whole account, so each of a player's characters sent the same totals and counted as another player; one player alone could make a band look confirmed. Identical totals now count once, in game and in the shipped data, and so do totals a player's characters sent at different times (3 or more bands exactly alike): only the biggest counts.

### Options
- **K opens on Professions**: a new option. On (the default), the K key opens Tradebook on the Professions tab as before. Off, K opens it on the tab you had open last (or on the profession whose window is open).

### Recipe list
- **Crafted item filters**: the recipe list's Filter menu can now narrow recipes by what they make, like the auction house: **only items this character can use**, **rarity** and **required level** (in steps of 5). Recipes that make no item, like enchants, are left out while one of these is chosen.
- **Pick several rarities or level ranges** (recipe list and Vendors tab): tick as many as you like, e.g. Uncommon and Rare, or 21-25 and 26-30. **Select all** at the top ticks them all, or clears them when they're all ticked. (The Vendors tab's rarity was "at least" one rarity; a saved choice carries over.)
- **Have materials > Except vendor items**: a new filter option that shows the recipes you have the gathered or crafted materials for, where only what a vendor sells (thread, vials, spices...) is missing. Recipes made only of vendor materials aren't shown. Herbs and other materials some vendors sell only a few of (limited stock) count as gathered, not as vendor items.

### Vendors
- **Questie's vendor lists are checked against real vendor windows**: when a vendor's window has been read (by you, in the community data, or by 2+ players sharing in game) and an item isn't in it, Questie's claim that the vendor sells it is no longer shown (e.g. Burkrum in Ashenvale doesn't sell Razor Arrow). ## v1.9.0

### Professions tab
- **A new Professions tab**, like the game's Professions book: your two primary profession slots (a blank box while one is free) and your secondary professions (Cooking, First Aid, Fishing; greyed out until learned), each with a large icon, rank and skill bar. Click one to open it, or drag it to an action bar for its spell (Alchemy, Cooking, Smelting for Mining...). Herbalism and Mining also have a smaller Find Herbs / Find Minerals icon at the right, above the skill bar: click it to start tracking (not in combat), or drag it on its own. The red Unlearn cross moved here too, next to the skill bar in each primary profession's box (it still opens the game's pop-up where you type UNLEARN). These replace the spell icons that were on each profession's tab, which leaves more room for the recipe list. The K key (and the profession micro button) always opens Tradebook on it. The minimap button and /tb open on it too when no profession window is open; turn that off in the options to open on the tab you had last.
- **Side tabs**: Professions, Characters, Legacy and Vendors are now icon tabs down the right side of the window (their name shows when you hover over them), which leaves the bottom row to the professions.

### Vendors
- **Vendor > Auction**: a new filter (needs Auctionator) finds items listed at the auction house for less than a vendor pays for them, e.g. Light Leather at 10c that sells to a vendor for 15c. It looks at any item, not only what vendors sell, shows what a vendor pays, the auction price and the difference, biggest difference first. Type a name, or browse them all without one; item type, rarity, level and usable still apply. The list is built once and kept until Auctionator's prices or your filters change, so it doesn't make the game stutter.

### Leveling plan
- **A sure path to the cap**: the plan now uses orange recipes (a skill-up every craft) wherever one can give the point, even when a yellow or green one would be cheaper on average, so following it gets you there with the crafts it lists. Only where no orange recipe is left does it use a yellow or green one; those steps say "craft about" and are marked as not a sure skill-up.

### Training
- **Nearest trainers for your recipes**: clicking the skill bar now also shows the nearest trainers where you can learn new recipes at your current rank (Karolek in Orgrimmar for Journeyman Leatherworking), not only the trainers for the next rank, which can be far away (Expert Leatherworking: Thunder Bluff). It's shown first until you can train the next rank, and when you're at the top rank.
- **Trainers that don't teach a recipe are left out**: a trainer whose window has been read (by you or the community) without a recipe is no longer listed under "Learn from" for it, even when the classic data names them (Godan in Thunder Bluff doesn't teach Enchant Shield - Lesser Stamina).
